title: Eurydice? More like “you better see!” #theatre #mayahawke #strangerth...
transcript: no I'm actually not okay right now because I just saw Maya Hawke play Eurydice not in Hadestown but in Sarah Ruhl’s play based on the same story and like all joking aside if you're a fan of Hadestown I actually think you have to see this because while it's obviously an extremely different take I think they both capture that same deep heartache at the core of this story and like I'm honestly struggling to convey just how magical I think this play is it has this blend of quirky humor with love and grief but presented with this quiet unassuming tenderness like this big operatic storm of emotions packaged in just the most delicate little glass box I should also mention this play was deeply formative for me personally I first discovered it actually before Hadestown in my freshman year of college while I was in the midst of both falling in love with and finding my personal taste in plays specifically I was really discovering my love for this stylized approach to playwriting where the writer has this hyper-distinct voice that really immerses you in the world and captures something more primal and profound about the human experience than I think naturalism ever could on top of all of that this production is so good I think it's kind of like a soft remount of the original production it's the same director and a lot of the same designers and then there's this cast which just like like ugh like it was just such a delight to see Maya Hawke play this role and Brian d’Arcy James was so good and then they cast my fave Caleb Eberhardt as Orpheus like they clearly revived this just for me personally and I don't know what I did to deserve this special treatment but whatever it is you're welcome because now you too have the opportunity to see this until June 22nd
classificationReason: Creator saw Maya Hawke in Eurydice production and compares to Hadestown, but this show is not on the provided list
